summary: Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Ngawang Samten (b. 1956) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Ganden Shartse Monastery, and served as Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–2019).
Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery and under Yeshe Paldrup, Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University (attested 2012) under Inder Mohan Singh and studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi, where K. T. S. Sarao served as his MA supervisor.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under teachers including Lianju Xia. He served as head of Central Broadcasting System and professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was a religious and Buddhist studies figure who founded Nipponzan-Myōhōji. He studied at Rissho University (1912), Taisho University, Kogi Shingonshu Rengo Daigaku, Horyu-ji, and Kennin-ji.

Nicholas Dirks (b. 1950) is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Wesleyan University (~1968–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981). He held posts at Caltech (~1986–1987), University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2012).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at New College, SOAS, and Oxford under Rodney Needham, and held posts at Durham, SOAS, Wolfson College, and the University of Oxford.

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University under Boris Vladimirtsov, he held professorships there, at the Institute of Oriental Studies, and at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts, founded the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute, and directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts.
Nicholas Witkowski works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from Stanford University (-2015) and held an appointment as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).
Nicholson T. Collier is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Bajetta is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a Doctoral Local Researcher at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026), where he also held an appointment as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter.

Nicola Di Cosmo (b. 1957) is a scholar of history, sinology, and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (~1984–1991) and served as Henry Luce Foundation Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study (~2003).

Nicolaas Johannes Krom (1883–1945) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held posts at Leiden University in 1919 and 1925–1945.
Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1903) and Moscow State University (~1903–1904). He held a post at Leiden University from 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004) and held a post at the University of Georgia.
